body.estimand_functional: \(\mathsf C(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sup}},\{X_i^{(m)}:m\in\mathcal E,\ i\le N_r\})=(\widehat{\mathcal G},\widehat H)\in\{(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I,\widetilde H):\mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widetilde H,P)\le\tau\}\cup\{\bot\},\quad r\ge r_0\)

sampling_model.design: A preliminary \(n\)-draw observational support batch is disjoint from the covariance streams and spans the deterministic support \(\mathcal S\) with probability one. Its span determines the canonical frame \(U\). Each environment then supplies one retained post-support stream; stage \(r\) uses exactly its first \(N_r=2^r\) coordinate observations \(Y_i^{(m)}=U^{\top}X_i^{(m)}\), so after stage zero only \(N_r-N_{r-1}\) new observations are appended. Stages before \(r_0=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\) sample only. At each \(r\ge r_0\), error \(\alpha\,2^{-r-1}\) is spent and the public transcript is restarted using the cumulative \(n\times n\) empirical covariances.
sampling_model.units: Independent centered Gaussian observations in each of the \(n+1\) environments, represented in fixed \(n\)-dimensional coordinates on the deterministic common support \(\mathcal S=\operatorname{col}(G)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Environment \(m\in[n]\) is one unknown-target stochastic perfect variance reset; environment \(0\) is observational.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is used; the relevant regularity is observed-covariance conditioning by \(\kappa\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For \(r\ge r_0\), cumulative \(n\times n\) empirical second moments from exactly \(N_r\) retained coordinate observations are inverted and mapped exactly to Gaussian score-correlation matrices under the induced laws \(P_m\); no inverse is attempted earlier and no learned score nuisance is required.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 5 and Theorem 1 select \(\eta\in(0,\eta^{\ast})\) with equation (22)'s all-subset eigenvalue minimum and \(\gamma\in(0,\gamma^{\ast})\) with equation (23)'s printed minimum norm product, under Assumption 1 and score-difference consistency.
For all non-empty subsets of intervention indices, Lemma 4.3 gives a uniform eigenvalue perturbation bound.
Our work develops confidence sequences whose widths go to zero, with nonasymptotic coverage guarantees under nonparametric conditions.
A single intervention on each latent variable is sufficient for identifiability.
Corollary 4.5 computes an approximate spectral projector within prescribed operator-norm error.

body.tldr: A fixed public rank-and-projector transcript, rather than all exponentially many subset sums, determines the finite-sample difficulty of the Acartürk et al. interventional causal representation learner. In fixed \(n\)-dimensional coordinates on the deterministic observation support, an anytime-valid Gaussian certificate retains one cumulative sample stream per environment, postpones every inverse until \(N_r\ge n\), and returns the transitive closure in observed intervention labels, \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\), together with an encoder whose rows use the same labels, or abstains. An all-dimension Gaussian bipartite family satisfies the source's printed equation (23) threshold condition, has valid reciprocal projector scale \(\rho^{\ast}(G)=1\), and meets all non-margin side conditions while keeping reached gaps constant and making equation (22)'s all-subset margin exponentially small. The remaining open content is an end-to-end polynomial-bit rational implementation of every spectral decision.

project_justification.gap: Acartürk et al.'s finite-sample graph-recovery premise combines equation (22)'s global all-subset margin \(\eta^{\ast}\), equation (23)'s printed norm-product scale \(\gamma^{\ast}\), Assumption 1, smooth full-support models, distinct interventions, and consistent score estimation. Its rank analysis still pays for every subset although the deterministic program executes only a polynomial transcript, and its printed norm product must not be identified with the reciprocal lower bound furnished by actual projector geometry.
project_justification.niche: A public query-local beta-min contract can separate statistical recoverability from post-selection thresholding while targeting only the graph and encoder class indexed by observed intervention labels.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a permutation-equivariant transcript-local certificate and, on the common subregion satisfying the reached projector band, a strict all-dimension relaxation of the source's equation (22) premise while retaining its printed equation (23) threshold condition and every non-margin side condition. The reciprocal quantity \(\rho_i(G)\) is reported separately as a valid lower bound, not imposed as a new class assumption. Certified polynomial-bit spectral composition remains the first-class open question.

body.related_work: Acartürk et al. (2024) are the sole strict finite-sample sufficient-condition comparator. Section 5 of the NeurIPS proceedings paper defines \(\eta^{\ast}\) in equation (22) as the minimum positive eigenvalue over all subset sums and prints \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\) in equation (23); Theorem 1 chooses thresholds strictly below those two quantities under Assumption 1 and score-difference consistency. The printed \(\gamma^{\ast}\) is not the reciprocal projector lower bound \(\rho^{\ast}\). Accordingly, Theorem 3 proves strict relaxation only of the all-subset spectral requirement on the common subregion already satisfying the reached projector band, while retaining the printed equation (23) threshold condition, smooth full support, intervention, parent-ratio, and score-consistency requirements. The reciprocal \(\rho_i(G)\) is a derived lower bound for each witnessed nonzero comparison rather than an added class assumption. No containment of the uncorrected published premise is claimed. Varıcı et al. (2025) supply the population score-difference range program that defines the transcript and are used as identification machinery rather than a tightening target. Squires et al. (2023) establish population linear causal disentanglement under one perfect intervention per node and validate the legal Gaussian subclass. Howard et al. (2021) provide time-uniform concentration machinery used to make stopping honest. Lee, Jin, and Aragam (2026) are adjacent context only: their unknown multi-node covariance model and subset reconstruction are not placed in a theorem-level inclusion relation with the present class. Uhler et al. (2013) establish cancellation geometry for observational partial correlations; the Gaussian separation theorem concerns score-correlation matrices reached by a latent-intervention transcript and makes no tightening claim against their result. The ICALP proceedings paper of Sobczyk (2025) is a summary; Corollary 4.5 in the April 27, 2025 arXiv full version, version 2, supplies a certified spectral-projector primitive for Open-ended Question 1. Dey et al. (2023) provide complementary bit-growth templates, but neither source gives the adaptive end-to-end bit theorem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theorem is an exact-real statistical statement. It guarantees distance to a unit-row population range class and parent support, not an invertible encoder, a unique eigenvector inside a repeated positive eigenspace, or a latent-coordinate error independent of \(\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\). The printed equation (23) norm product does not itself control actual projector comparisons; the comparison theorem therefore holds the reached projector band fixed and relaxes only equation (22). The bit-complexity result remains open and may require sharper interval bounds for projector-product norms than black-box eigensolver accuracy alone.
body.honest_scope: Theorems 1, 2, and 3 are posed on the linear Gaussian perfect-intervention subclass in fixed coordinates on \(\mathcal S\) and target only \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and the correspondingly environment-indexed ambient encoder class; no labelled latent graph is asserted to be a functional of \(P\). Lee, Jin, and Aragam (2026) are adjacent rather than a theorem-level comparator. Theorem 3 gives a strict fixed-margin relaxation of Acartürk et al.'s equation (22) requirement only on the common subregion satisfying the reached projector band; it retains their printed equation (23) threshold condition and all non-margin side conditions. The valid reciprocal \(\rho_i(G)\) is derived by Proposition 1 and is not a new assumption. The theorem does not claim that the printed norm product lower-bounds projector comparisons or that the uncorrected published sufficient region is contained in the transcript-local class. The result is not a minimax lower bound or a claim that the source's qualitative premise fails. When uncertainty radii vanish, Proposition 2 reduces the certificate to the known population program. No claim is made that \(g_0\) and \(h_0\) are jointly necessary for every causal representation learner.
